# yoloabdo.com — Abdelrahman Eita

> Abdelrahman Eita (also known as "yoloabdo") is a Staff Software Engineer based in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with 10+ years of iOS and Apple-platform development experience. He has published five apps on the App Store: Sajdah (also spelled Sajda; Quran for Apple TV), Tally (Apple TV scoreboard), Capybara Rush (iPhone reflex game), Wi-Fi QR (guest Wi-Fi QR code maker and printable sign app), and Tateemi (Arabic vaccination tracker). Three more are in public TestFlight beta and coming soon to the App Store: Angry Nona: Night Shift (iPhone nanny game), ColorTalk (iPad ABC coloring app for children 5 and under), and SwingCoach (iPhone kettlebell swing coach). This file describes him and each app for AI search citation. He also makes free browser projects: How Surfing Works (an interactive 3D surfing explainer) and Drive Town (a 3D driving game to practise the Dutch car theory exam).

## About Abdelrahman Eita

- Role: Staff Software Engineer, specializing in iOS, SwiftUI, The Composable Architecture (TCA), and modular architecture
- Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands
- Career: shipped apps at Bleacher Report, Niceone, Iqraaly, NewStore, and Marktplaats (eBay); GoChat reached #1 on the US App Store with 1M+ users in 7 days; Iqraaly, an audiobook app, passed 500K downloads and reached the top 10 on the App Store in Egypt; across these apps, his work is used by millions of people
- Community: founder of SwiftCairo (Egypt's largest iOS community, 1,000+ members) and LintSchool; 50+ developers mentored across both
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Sajdah (Sajda) - Quran, Prayer Times & Athan for Apple TV

> Sajdah (App Store name "Sajdah: Quran & Athan TV", also spelled Sajda) is a Quran, prayer and remembrance app for Apple TV (tvOS 17 or later). It is free to download, with 200+ reciters, verse-by-verse and word-by-word tracking, Quran fonts, prayer times with 13 athan voices, Qibla direction, the Prayer Screen (full-screen prayer times in six styles, formerly Prayer Room), morning and evening adhkar, the verse and hadith of the day, Quran radio, live Islamic TV including Makkah, and Top Shelf cards on the Apple TV Home Screen.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/)
- Languages: [English](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/) · [العربية](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/ar/) · [Türkçe](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/tr/) · [Français](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/fr/) · [Español](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/es/) · [اردو](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/ur/) · [বাংলা](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/bn/) · [Bahasa Indonesia](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/id/) · [Русский](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/ru/) · [Svenska](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/sv/) · [中文](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/zh/)
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6759179587)
- [The Prayer Screen on Apple TV](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-prayer-screen-apple-tv/): the six full-screen Prayer Screen styles (Classic, Focus, Horizon, Timetable, Rosette, Board), Arabic layout, burn-in protection, and the free preview
- [Sajdah 1.6.0 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-6-0-release-notes/): a new Today screen, the Prayer Screen in six Premium styles with a free preview, the Athan in 13 voices (Premium), new Adhkar art, a What's New screen
- [Sajdah 1.5.0 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-5-0-release-notes/)
- [The best Quran apps for Apple TV, compared (2026)](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/quran-apps-apple-tv-compared/): nine Quran apps that run on Apple TV, compared on the TV experience, with sources
- [The journey so far: building Sajdah for Apple TV](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/building-sajdah-apple-tv-journey/)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/support/) · [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/privacy/) · [Privacy Policy in Arabic](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/privacy/ar/)

## Key Features

- **200+ Quran Reciters** with multiple narrations (Hafs, Warsh, and others)
- **Verse-by-Verse Sync** with precise ayah tracking, and **word-by-word highlighting** on selected Hafs reciters (premium)
- **Quran Fonts**: Uthmanic (free), plus Amiri, Scheherazade New, Noto Naskh, KFGQPC Nastaleeq and Lateef (premium)
- **Live Tab**: Quran radio stations with a live equalizer and live Islamic TV channels, including Makkah (premium)
- **Today** (free): the verse of the day at the center, the next prayer in a one-line prayer bar, and short cards for continue listening, Adhkar and the hadith of the day in the app language
- **Morning and Evening Adhkar** with a Siri Remote counter
- **Prayer Times** for Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha in the location's time zone, **13 Athan voices** plus a Fajr Athan, and **Qibla Direction** (premium)
- **Prayer Screen** (formerly Prayer Room): full-screen prayer times that stay on the TV, in six styles (premium; free users can watch a preview)
- **Top Shelf**: continue listening, verse of the day and next prayer on the Apple TV Home Screen
- **Player**: focus mode, ambient mode, sleep timer (15-60 min or end of surah), repeat and A-B repeat, playback speed from 0.5x to 2x, translations and optional transliteration
- **Multilingual**: English, Arabic, Turkish, French, Spanish, Urdu, Bengali, Indonesian, Russian, Swedish, and Chinese

## Pricing

- Free: Quran recitation with every reciter, verse-by-verse reading with synchronized Arabic text, one translation, surah repeat, sleep timer, the Today screen with the next prayer time, morning and evening Adhkar
- Sajdah Premium (optional in-app subscription): Quran radio, live TV, the full prayer schedule with the Athan in 13 voices, Qibla direction, the Prayer Screen in all six styles, ambient mode, all translations and transliteration, word-by-word highlighting, memorization tools, playback speed, extra Quran fonts
- No ads

## Platform

- Apple TV (tvOS 17 or later)
- Requires internet connection for streaming

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Tally - Apple TV Scoreboard and Game Night Score Keeper

> Tally is a free Apple TV scoreboard app and game night score keeper built for the living room. It supports 6 sports plus Game Night mode for 2-8 players, with giant room-readable scores, timers, live score tracking, turn markers, undo, and a big-screen winner reveal. Sports include basketball, soccer, tennis, ping pong, volleyball, and a generic custom mode. Game Night mode supports Running Total, Rounds Won, and Lives. Since version 1.3.2 (28 August 2026), every feature is free, with no subscriptions, in-app purchases, ads, or analytics.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/)
- [Trailer](https://yoloabdo.com/media/tally/tally-v13-promo-1080.mp4)
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tally-game-night-scoreboard/id6760623633)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/privacy/)
- [Tally 1.3.2 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/tally-1-3-2-release-notes/): Tally is now fully free; every sport and Game Night unlocked; no analytics

## Key Features

- **6 Sports + Game Night** — Basketball (quarters, 1/2/3-point), Soccer (halves, stoppage time), Tennis (game/set/match, deuce/advantage, tiebreaks), Ping Pong (best of 5, serve rotation), Volleyball (rally-point, final set to 15), Generic (custom). Game Night mode: 2-8 players, three scoring models (Running Total, Rounds Won, Lives), turn marker, MVP badge, Play Again
- **Giant Scores** — 220pt typography readable from across the room
- **Live Score Tracking + Timers** — Countdown (basketball), countup (soccer), buzzer on expiration, and quick score updates on the big screen
- **Full Undo** — Revert any scoring action, up to 20 steps back
- **Custom Team Names** — Set before each game, saved automatically
- **Dark & Light Mode** — Follows Apple TV appearance, OLED-friendly
- **Controls Overlay** — Press Menu for undo, point values, timer controls, end game
- **Audio Feedback** — Score sounds, timer buzzer, game over fanfare
- **VoiceOver** — Full accessibility with score announcements
- **Onboarding** — First-launch walkthrough for Siri Remote controls

## Pricing

- Completely free since version 1.3.2 (28 August 2026)
- No subscriptions, in-app purchases, paywalls, or ads
- No analytics: the app collects no data

## Platform

- Apple TV (tvOS 17+)
- Works on Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD
- No internet required — works fully offline

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Capybara Rush: Swipe Fast - Cozy iPhone Reflex Game

> Capybara Rush: Swipe Fast is a cozy iPhone reflex game built for quick 30-second rounds. Players read prompts, swipe in the correct direction, keep combos alive, trigger Fever Rush, grab golden bonuses, earn coins, unlock capybara skins, and compare high scores with Game Center. It works offline and includes no ads, no tracking, and no account requirement.

## Links

## Key Features

- **30-Second Swipe Rounds** — quick one-thumb arcade sessions
- **Prompt Twists** — normal prompts, fake prompts, and opposite prompts
- **Fever Rush** — strong runs fill a meter and shift into faster scoring
- **Golden Bonuses** — special moments worth more score and coins
- **Unlockable Skins** — Sleepy, Strawberry, Sunglasses, Wizard, Space, and Golden capybara styles
- **Game Center** — leaderboard support for high scores
- **Offline Friendly** — progress, coins, best score, skins, tutorial state, and settings are stored locally
- **Privacy-First** — no ads, no tracking, no account, and no personal data collection

# Wi-Fi QR - Guest Wi-Fi QR Codes and Printable Signs

> Wi-Fi QR is a private iPhone and iPad utility for creating guest Wi-Fi QR codes, Airbnb WiFi signs, and printable guest Wi-Fi signs. It is built for hosts, homes, cafes, offices, guest rooms, short-term rentals, VRBO stays, vacation rentals, and Airbnb-style stays. It helps people who are searching for an Airbnb WiFi sign template, WiFi QR code template, WiFi password sign, editable Canva WiFi template, Etsy WiFi QR sign, house manual WiFi instructions, welcome binder WiFi page, or guest network QR code. It can start from the current Wi-Fi network name, add hidden or manual networks, scan router-label or printed password text, save trusted networks locally, search saved networks, share QR code images, and print or export sign PDFs in six templates and four paper sizes. Version 1.7 (October 2026) adds WPA or WEP checks, signs that fit long passwords, and Arabic router-sticker labels. Free, with no account, no ads and no in-app purchases; anonymous usage events through Firebase Analytics never include Wi-Fi names, passwords or QR contents.

## Links

- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6776169783)
- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/)
- [The story behind Wi-Fi QR](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-story/): why the app exists, from a hotel Wi-Fi card in London to the App Store in four days, built with Codex
- [Wi-Fi QR 1.7 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-1-7-release-notes/): WPA or WEP with clear checks, guest signs that fit long passwords, better router-sticker scanning
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **Generate Guest Wi-Fi QR Codes** - create scannable codes for WPA/WPA2/WPA3, WEP, open, and hidden networks, with inline checks for the network name and password
- **Printable Guest Wi-Fi Signs** - six templates (Classic, Code Only, Gallery Placard, Concierge Ledger, Signal Grid, Ink-Safe Editorial) in 4 x 6 in, 5 x 7 in, A4 and US Letter; long names and passwords shrink and wrap to fit; print from the share sheet
- **Airbnb and VRBO Host Use Cases** - create WiFi password signs for welcome binders, house manuals, check-in instructions, fridges, TV stands, desks, and router shelves
- **Template Search Replacement** - useful for people searching Etsy, Canva, or Pinterest for WiFi QR code templates and printable Airbnb WiFi signs
- **Router Sticker Scanning** - scan printed router-sticker or password-card text with the camera, including English, German, French and Arabic labels, and review it before saving
- **Use Current Network Name** - with permission, reads the current Wi-Fi SSID to reduce typing
- **Manual and Hidden Networks** - supports manual SSID entry, open guest networks, and hidden-network QR codes
- **Saved Networks** - stores trusted networks locally on the device for quick reuse
- **Search** - finds saved networks quickly from the tab bar
- **Share QR Images and Sign PDFs** - exports QR images and printable guest signs through the iOS share sheet
- **Privacy** - no accounts, ads or cross-app tracking; saved networks stay on the device; anonymous usage events (Firebase Analytics) never include Wi-Fi names, passwords, QR contents, scanned text or sign text

## Pricing

- Free
- No ads, no subscription, no in-app purchases

## Platform

- iOS 17+ for iPhone and iPad
- Works offline for saved/manual networks; current Wi-Fi name detection uses iOS location permission

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# تطعيمي (Tateemi) - Vaccination Tracker

> Tateemi is a free Arabic vaccination tracker for iPhone with country-based child immunization schedules. Parents choose the supported country schedule, add a child with their birth date, and the app calculates upcoming doses, tracks vaccination progress, sends smart reminders, provides medical information for each vaccine, supports multiple children, and stores all data locally on-device only.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/tateemi/)
- [English Page](https://yoloabdo.com/tateemi/en/)
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tateemi-baby-vaccine-tracker/id6760822504)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/tateemi/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/tateemi/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **Country-Based Schedules** with dose timelines calculated from the child's birth date
- **Vaccination Progress Tracking** with visual completion percentage for each child
- **Smart Reminders** — notifications 1 week, 3 days, and on the day of each upcoming dose
- **Medical Information** for each vaccine: what it is, why it matters, and possible side effects
- **Multiple Children Support** — track all your children's vaccinations in one place
- **Offline / Local Data Only** — all data stored on-device, no servers, no tracking, no account required

## Pricing

- Free (no subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases)

## Platform

- iOS (iPhone), requires iOS 17+
- Works fully offline — no internet required

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Angry Nona: Night Shift - Cozy iPhone Nanny Game (TestFlight Beta)

> Angry Nona: Night Shift is a cozy iPhone game. Six toddlers. One nanny. The player keeps a nursery asleep from 9 PM until dawn: shh kids who stir, fetch the bottle, teddy, or story they ask for, queue several taps in a row, do chores in quiet moments, and keep Princess Nona from waking the room. It has 13 nights plus Endless (Nights 1-4 free; one Full Shift purchase unlocks the rest), a Nanny shop that runs on points earned in play, and nanny outfits. No ads and no tracking. It is not on the App Store yet.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/angry-nona/)
- [TestFlight Beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/bvBDeeQ5)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/angry-nona/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/angry-nona/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **Six Toddlers, One Nanny** - keep every crib asleep through the night shift
- **Shh and Fetch** - read each kid's bubble; shh them, or bring a bottle, a teddy, or a story
- **Tap Queue** - tap several cribs in a row and the nanny serves them one by one
- **Chores in Quiet Moments** - warm a bottle, crochet a teddy, or water the plant
- **Coffee** - keeps the nanny going on long nights
- **Mom's Calls** - decline fast, or the phone rings in the nursery
- **Princess Nona** - the ringleader with a crown; if she wakes, the room can follow
- **13 Nights + Endless** - nights add kids and twists, then Endless for high scores. Nights 1-4 free; Full Shift unlocks the rest
- **Nanny Shop** - spend points earned in play on helps and new looks
- **Outfits** - dress the nanny in new looks
- **Accessibility** - VoiceOver and Reduce Motion support
- **Privacy-First** - no ads, no tracking, no account; only anonymous game stats and crash reports

## Availability

- Public TestFlight beta: https://testflight.apple.com/join/bvBDeeQ5
- Coming soon to the App Store
- Pricing will be announced at launch

## Platform

- iOS (iPhone), requires iOS 18+
- Plays fully offline; progress, settings, and points are stored on the device

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# ColorTalk: ABC Kids Coloring - Learn the Alphabet & Words on iPad (TestFlight Beta)

> ColorTalk is an ABC coloring app for iPad that teaches children 5 and under the English alphabet. The child picks a letter, colors its page, and meets the letter and one word: "C is for cow." X is the one exception: "Fox ends with X." It works offline. No ads, no accounts, no tracking. ColorTalk sends no analytics or crash reports. It has no in-app purchases and no external links. It is not on the App Store yet.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/colortalk/)
- [TestFlight Beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/4jjubyD7)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/colortalk/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/colortalk/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **One Letter, One Word** - each page teaches one letter and one word, such as "C is for cow"
- **Coloring First** - coloring is the main activity; the letter and its word support the art
- **Lumo the Firefly** - says the letters, words, and prompts in recorded voice clips; spoken prompts are off by default, and a parent turns them on in Settings
- **Parents Area** - behind a grown-up question; holds Settings and local progress
- **Works Offline** - all pages, words, and prompts are bundled in the app
- **Privacy** - No ads, no accounts, no tracking. ColorTalk sends no analytics or crash reports. Optional voice answers (off by default) use on-device speech recognition and save no audio

## Availability

- Public TestFlight beta: https://testflight.apple.com/join/4jjubyD7
- Coming soon to the App Store
- Kids category, ages 5 and under

## Platform

- iPadOS (iPad), landscape only, English only

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# SwingCoach: Kettlebell Workout - Kettlebell Swing Rep Counter and Form Check for iPhone (TestFlight Beta)

> SwingCoach is a kettlebell workout app for the Russian swing. The iPhone camera counts each rep and checks your form. When a fault repeats, a short spoken cue tells you what to fix. It starts you with a five-swing form check and a three-session starter plan. An Apple Watch app is optional. Free, with no account, no ads and no in-app purchases. Pose analysis runs on the iPhone; no video is recorded or uploaded. SwingCoach is in public TestFlight beta and coming soon to the App Store.

## Links

- [Landing Page](https://yoloabdo.com/swingcoach/)
- [TestFlight Beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/Yk2ZgDkn)
- [Support](https://yoloabdo.com/swingcoach/support/)
- [Privacy Policy](https://yoloabdo.com/swingcoach/privacy/)

## Key Features

- **Live Rep Count** - the camera finds your hips, knees and arms and counts each swing; fix the count with one tap
- **Spoken Form Cues** - a short cue when a fault repeats
- **Five-Swing Check** - one clear place to focus and a three-session starter plan
- **Train Your Way** - open training, or a rep goal of 10, 20, 30, 50 or your own count
- **Rep Review** - the deepest hinge and the final lockout of each rep, with hip, knee and arm angles, plus History
- **Apple Watch, Optional** - heart rate, active calories, workout control and Apple Health

## Availability

- Public TestFlight beta: https://testflight.apple.com/join/Yk2ZgDkn
- Coming soon to the App Store

## Platform

- iOS (iPhone), requires iOS 17+; the optional Apple Watch app needs watchOS 10+

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# How Surfing Works - Interactive 3D Explainer

> How Surfing Works is a free, interactive 3D explainer by Abdelrahman Eita that runs in the browser. It covers where waves come from, why they break, the anatomy of a wave, beach, point and reef breaks, how to read a surf report, how to ride a wave, when to pop up, and surf safety including rip currents. Visitors can watch it as a short film, change the wind and seabed, try a pop-up timing game, and record a video.

## Links

- [How Surfing Works](https://yoloabdo.com/surfing/)

# Drive Town - Dutch Car Theory Exam Practice in 3D

> Drive Town is a free 3D driving game by Abdelrahman Eita for learners who prepare for the Dutch car theory exam (CBR theorie-examen auto, category B). It runs in the browser on desktop and phone. The player drives a learner car through a small Dutch town with assisted steering and decides the speed, the indicators, when to wait, when to merge and when to overtake. It has 24 lessons in 7 chapters, a mock exam in the current CBR format (50 questions in 30 minutes, with a pass at 44), a hazard-perception practice and Dutch exam terms. It is an independent practice project and is not made by or linked to CBR.

## Links

- [Play Drive Town](https://yoloabdo.com/drive-town/)
- [Exam guide and Dutch terms](https://yoloabdo.com/drive-town/guide/)
- [3D artwork credits](https://yoloabdo.com/drive-town/credits.html)

## Key Features

- **24 driving lessons in 7 chapters** — Bakery run (speed, priority from the right, zebra crossings, cyclists, parking), Signs & signals (traffic lights, STOP, shark teeth and signed priority, a changing speed limit), Sharing the road (buses leaving a stop, narrow roads, railway crossings), Roundabouts (entering, signalling out, cyclists on the cycle path), Merging (zipper merge, joining from an acceleration lane, making room), Lights & sirens (amber light, emergency vehicles, police instructions), Trams & bikes (trams, cycle lanes, overtaking)
- **Mock exam** — 50 questions in 30 minutes with a pass at 44, like the CBR car theory exam since 7 April 2025. Six question types: Ja/Nee, multiple choice, multiple response, number, tap a marker in a picture, and put in order. Picture questions play a short 3D clip and stop at the key moment. The screen uses the exam terms Vraag x van y, Resterende tijd, Markeren and Overzicht. The bank has 193 original questions in eight exam topics, each with an explanation and an official source
- **Hazard practice** — 61 short 3D clips, 25 per run, with the answers Brake, Release accelerator or Do nothing. It is based on the former CBR hazard-perception part (gevaarherkenning, used until 6 April 2025)
- **Feedback and replay** — every lesson ends with a rule check; a mistake shows the recorded speed and position, with a replay of the decision moment
- **Weak topics** — mistakes from the mock exam, the hazard practice and the lessons are counted per topic. On the result, "Practise lessons" (mock exam) or "Practise this" (hazard test) opens the matching lesson, and "Hazard clips" opens its clips
- **Dutch exam terms** — 115 words such as voorrang verlenen (give way), haaientanden (shark teeth), ritsen (zipper merge) and invoegen (merging in), shown next to the English
- **Guided and Independent modes** — coach prompts, or varied traffic with no safety hints

## Pricing

- Free, with no account, ads or in-app purchases

## Platform

- Any modern browser with WebGL, on desktop and phone
- Interface in English, with Dutch exam terms
- Game progress is saved only in the browser. The published page counts visits with Google Analytics, like the rest of this site

## Limits

- Practice only: a mock exam result does not predict a real exam result
- Rules link to the Dutch traffic law (RVV 1990) and other official sources. A driving instructor has not yet reviewed every question and clip
- Drive Town is not made by, endorsed by or linked to CBR

## Developer

- Built by Abdelrahman Eita
- Contact: abdulrhman.eaita@gmail.com

# Full text

Product · Sajdah for Apple TV

# The Prayer Screen: prayer times that look good on your TV all day

Most TVs sit dark between shows. With Sajdah, the biggest screen at home can show the day's prayers instead, in a design that fits the room.

![The Horizon style of the Prayer Screen: Dhuhr is next in 1:23:45, the prayers sit on the arc of the sun across the day, and a small chip says: swipe up or down to change style, Back to exit.](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-prayer-screen-apple-tv/prayer-screen-horizon-1280.webp)

In many homes, the prayer times live on a phone. You unlock it, open an app, and look for the next prayer. In a masjid it is different: the times hang on the wall, and everyone in the room can see them. I wanted that feeling at home, on the screen the whole family already looks at.

That is the **Prayer Screen** in [Sajdah, the Quran and Athan app for Apple TV](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/). It shows the day's prayer times full screen, with a live countdown to the next prayer, and it stays on between prayers.

## How it works

Open the Prayer Screen from its tile on the Today screen. Swipe up or down on the remote to change the style. Press Back to leave. The hint chip goes away after four seconds, and Sajdah remembers the last style you picked.

## Six styles

Every style shows the next prayer, a countdown to it, all six times of the day (Fajr, Sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha), and the Hijri and Gregorian dates.

- **Classic**: dark green, the next prayer in a large serif, a gold countdown, and the six times in one row.
- **Focus**: deep navy, with a gold ring that fills as the time between two prayers passes.
- **Horizon**: the path of the sun across the day, with each prayer on the arc and a dot for the time now. It opens first.
- **Timetable**: the next prayer large on the left, and a table of prayers in English and Arabic on the right, with a progress bar.
- **Rosette**: the day as a dial, with the Arabic name of the next prayer in the center.
- **Board**: a black departure board with numbered rows and a status for each prayer: passed, next, or time left.

![The Classic style.](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-prayer-screen-apple-tv/prayer-screen-classic-1280.webp)

![The Board style in Arabic, right to left with Arabic digits.](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-prayer-screen-apple-tv/prayer-screen-board-arabic-1280.webp)

## Made to read from the sofa

Each style puts the name of the next prayer and the countdown first, large enough to read from across the room. Passed prayers are dimmer. The digits have equal width, so they do not jump. The colors are dark and soft for a room at night.

## In Arabic, too

When the Apple TV is in Arabic, the Prayer Screen reads right to left, with Arabic names, dates and digits.

## Safe to leave on all day

- It keeps the Apple TV awake while it is open.
- Every two minutes, the content moves a few points along a small oval, to help protect OLED TVs from burn-in.
- After ten minutes with no remote press, it dims to 70% brightness. Any button brings it back.

## Free preview and Premium

All six styles are part of Sajdah Premium. Without Premium, you can watch a free preview in Horizon with the real times for your city. Other styles show a Premium chip; press Select to see the Premium options, or Horizon comes back after 30 seconds. Premium also adds the Athan in 13 voices at every prayer.

Release notes · Sajdah for Apple TV

# Sajdah 1.6.0: a new Today screen, the Prayer Screen and the Athan in 13 voices

A calmer home screen built around the verse of the day, prayer times you can leave on the TV, and the Athan at every prayer in the voice you love.

![The Masjid al-Haram in Makkah lit up at night, under a Premium label and the words: The Athan, on time, at home. 13 beautiful voices. Every prayer, on your TV.](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-6-0-release-notes/sajdah-1-6-0-athan-1280.webp)

Sajdah (سجدة) 1.6.0 is out for the [Quran and Athan app for Apple TV](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/). This update is about the moments around prayer: what you see when you open the app, what stays on the TV between prayers, and the call to prayer itself. Here is everything that changed.

## In short

- A new Today screen with the verse of the day at the center
- The Prayer Screen: full-screen prayer times in 6 styles
- The Athan in 13 voices at every prayer
- New art for the morning and evening Adhkar
- A What's New screen after each update
- Many design and Arabic text fixes

## A calmer Today screen

Today is the first thing you see when you open Sajdah, so it should feel quiet. In 1.6.0 the **verse of the day** sits at the center of the screen, with room to read it from the sofa.

Your **next prayer** now lives in a prayer bar that takes one line, so you can see the time without a large panel in the way. Below it, shorter cards take you to the rest of your day:

- **Continue listening** from the surah where you stopped.
- **Adhkar** for the morning and the evening.
- The **hadith of the day**.

The Today screen and your next prayer time are free.

## The Prayer Screen

The Prayer Room is now called the **Prayer Screen**. It shows the day's prayer times full screen and stays on your TV, so the whole room can see the times between prayers.

There are **6 styles** to choose from, and all of them are part of Sajdah Premium. If you do not have Premium, you can watch a free preview first and then decide if you want to upgrade.

## The Athan, on time, at home

With Sajdah Premium, the Athan plays at every prayer on your Apple TV. Pick your favorite of **13 voices**, and Sajdah uses it for each prayer of the day.

## New art for the morning and evening Adhkar

The morning and evening Adhkar cards have new art: a drawn desert at dawn for the morning, and the same desert at dusk for the evening. The Adhkar stay free.

## A What's New screen

After an update, Sajdah now shows a short What's New screen, so you can see what changed without a visit to the App Store.

## Design and Arabic text fixes

This release also has many small fixes to the design across the app, and to how Arabic text shows on the TV.

![A father and his young son sit together on a sofa in a dim living room and watch a softly glowing TV, next to the words: Pass the Quran down.](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-6-0-release-notes/sajdah-1-6-0-family-1280.webp)

_One calm app for the whole family, on the biggest screen at home._

## What is free and what is Premium

Sajdah stays free to download. Quran recitation, verse-by-verse reading, the Today screen with your next prayer time, and the Adhkar are free.

**Sajdah Premium** adds the Athan in 13 voices, the full prayer schedule and Qibla direction, the Prayer Screen in all 6 styles, Quran radio and live TV, Ambient Quran Mode, memorization tools such as verse repeat, A-B repeat and playback speed, word-by-word highlighting, all translation languages and transliteration, and the extra Quran fonts.

## How to update

If automatic app updates are on, your Apple TV installs Sajdah 1.6.0 by itself. You can also open the App Store on your Apple TV, find Sajdah, and choose Update. To see what came before, read the [Sajdah 1.5.0 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-5-0-release-notes/). Questions or ideas? Write to me through [Sajdah support](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/support/).

Release notes · Tally for Apple TV

# Tally 1.3.2: the Apple TV scoreboard is now fully free

Every sport and Game Night mode are now unlocked for everyone. No subscription, no paywall, no ads, and no analytics.

![The Tally home screen on Apple TV: Start Game Night and six sports, with nothing locked](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/tally-1-3-2-release-notes/tally-1-3-2-home-1280.webp)

[Tally](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/) is a scoreboard app for Apple TV. You keep score with the Siri Remote, and the whole room sees giant numbers on the TV. Version 1.3.2 came out on **28 August 2026**, and it makes one big change: Tally is now completely free.

## In short

- Everything is unlocked: all sports, Game Night, timers and player colors
- If you paid for Pro, you do not need to do anything
- No analytics: the app now collects no data
- Siri Remote focus fixes

## Everything is unlocked

Before 1.3.2, the free version had Basketball and the Generic scoreboard. The other sports, Game Night mode, the round timer and the player colors needed Tally Pro. Now there is no Pro. You get all of it:

- **Six sports with real rules:** Basketball, Soccer, Tennis, Ping Pong, Volleyball and a Generic scoreboard for any game.
- **Game Night mode** for 2–8 players, with custom names and eight colors.
- **Three ways to score Game Night:** Running Total, Rounds Won and Lives.
- **Timers:** game clocks for the sports, and an optional 5 or 10-minute countdown for Game Night.
- **The finish:** ranked standings, an MVP badge and Play Again with the same players.

There are no subscriptions, in-app purchases, paywalls or ads. The upgrade screens and the Tally Pro row in Settings are gone.

![Tally Game Night on Apple TV with eight players, each in their own color, and Player 1 to play](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/tally-1-3-2-release-notes/tally-1-3-2-game-night-1280.webp)

## If you paid for Tally Pro

Thank you. You keep everything, and you do not need to do anything. Settings still has a **Restore Purchases** row if you want it, but the app no longer needs a purchase to unlock a feature.

## No analytics

Tally no longer includes Firebase. The app has no analytics, no ads, no accounts and no tracking. Your team names and settings stay on your Apple TV. The [privacy policy](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/privacy/) now says this.

## Fixes

The Siri Remote focus works better on the first-launch screens. Focus now lands where you expect it, so you can start your first game faster.

## How to play with the Siri Remote

- Swipe left or right to pick a team or a player.
- Press Select to score.
- Press Play/Pause to start or stop the clock. In Game Night, it moves to the next turn.
- Press Menu for the controls overlay. Hold Menu for a quick undo.

## How to get it

Tally needs tvOS 17 or later, and it works on Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD. If automatic updates are on, your Apple TV installs 1.3.2 by itself. If you are new, find Tally in the App Store on your Apple TV and download it for free. Questions or ideas? Write to me through [Tally support](https://yoloabdo.com/tally/support/).

Release notes · Capybara Rush for iPhone

# Capybara Rush 1.5: daily runs, the Capybara Cup and a poster of your best run

One 30-second run a day that counts, a four-week Cup from 11 November, and a poster that dares your friends to beat your score.

![Capybara Rush 1.5: the Home screen with the daily challenge ticket, a Capybara Cup share poster, and a results screen with Cup progress](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/capybara-rush-1-5-release-notes/capybara-rush-1-5-cup-1280.webp)

[Capybara Rush](https://yoloabdo.com/capybara-rush/) is a cozy swipe game for iPhone. A round lasts 30 seconds: an arrow appears, and you swipe that way before time runs out. Version 1.5 gives you a reason to come back every day, and a reason to show your friends. Here is what is new.

## In short

- A daily run with its own Game Center board from 21 October
- The Capybara Cup: four weeks, 11 November to 8 December
- A poster of your run to share or save to Photos
- Six Game Center achievements
- A clearer results screen
- One optional question about how you found the game

## One daily run that counts

The Home screen now has a **Daily challenge** ticket. Every day has a level, Cozy, Flow or Rush, and every player gets the same arrows that day. Your timing still shapes the round, so no two runs are the same.

- **Your first attempt each day counts.** It goes to the daily Game Center board. The attempt is used when the round starts, so quitting halfway does not give you a second try.
- After that, you can play the daily again for practice. Practice runs still count for your all-time best and your streak.
- The ticket has seven stamps, one for each day you play. Your streak earns badges at 4, 7 and 14 days.
- You can turn on a reminder at 19:00 your time, if you want one.

The daily Game Center board starts on **21 October 2026** and resets every day.

## The Capybara Cup: four weeks from 11 November

The Capybara Cup runs for four weeks, from **11 November to 8 December 2026**:

- Week 1: 11–17 November
- Week 2: 18–24 November
- Week 3: 25 November – 1 December
- Week 4: 2–8 December

During the Cup, the daily run is the Cup run. Your first attempt each day also counts on the weekly **Capybara Cup** board in Game Center. Cup days follow your own local date. The results screen shows how many Cup dailies you have played. Finish five to earn the **Cup Finisher** badge and a gold frame on your poster.

## A poster of your run

After a run, tap **Share poster**. The poster shows your capybara, your grade, your score, your accuracy and combo, the coins you earned and your fever count. At the bottom it asks “Can you beat” your score, with a QR code your friends can scan to get the game. You can send it with the share sheet or save it to Photos. A Cup run gets a stamp with the week and the level.

## Six Game Center achievements

- **First Splash**: play your first round.
- **Daily Debut**: play your first daily run.
- **Weekly Finisher**: fill all seven daily stamps.
- **Survivor**: score in Survival mode.
- **Full Wardrobe**: collect the seven original skins, from Classic to Golden.
- **Century**: play 100 rounds.

## A clearer results screen

The results screen now makes the next step obvious. **Play again** is the big button, with a goal such as “Only 120 to your best”. On your first daily run, or when you set a new best, **Share poster** takes its place. Below it, the row has Play again, Share, Scores and Home. Scores opens the board for the run you just played.

![Capybara Rush gameplay with a Swipe Down prompt, the Home screen with the optional how-did-you-find-us card, and the skin collection](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/capybara-rush-1-5-release-notes/capybara-rush-1-5-play-1280.webp)

## One quick, optional question

The Home screen may ask once: “How did you find Capybara Rush?” You can pick a friend or challenge, App Store search, the Games app or Game Center, an event or feature, or Other. Or tap the X and it goes away. The answer helps me learn where new players come from.

## The game, if you are new

Each round lasts 30 seconds. Swipe the way the arrow points. Later in the round, twists appear: swipe the *opposite* way, or any way *except* the one shown. Correct swipes build a combo and fill the Fever meter, which doubles your points for five seconds. Golden prompts give bonus points and coins. Pick Cozy, Flow or Rush, or try Survival, which has no clock and ends after three mistakes. Spend your coins on capybara skins.

## Price

Capybara Rush is free, with no ads, no in-app purchases and no account. Coins come only from play. Game Center is optional. The game collects anonymous usage statistics only, and it does not track you across other apps.

## How to update

If automatic updates are on, your iPhone installs Capybara Rush 1.5 by itself. You can also open the App Store, find Capybara Rush, and tap Update. Sign in to Game Center to post your daily runs to the boards. Questions or ideas? Write to me through [Capybara Rush support](https://yoloabdo.com/capybara-rush/support/).

Story · Wi-Fi QR for iPhone

# From a hotel Wi-Fi card to the App Store: the story behind Wi-Fi QR

I built a small app for one problem I had in a London hotel. Four days later it was on the App Store, and people I never met started to use it too.

![Three iPhone screens: the first version of WiFi QR on 31 May with a list of saved networks, and Wi-Fi QR today with a QR code to share and a printable guest sign](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-story/wifi-qr-then-now-1280.webp)

I was on a trip to London. When I got to the hotel, the Wi-Fi name and password were written on a card. So I did what everyone does: I typed a long password by hand, one letter at a time.

I knew that Android has a better way. On an Android phone, you can open the Wi-Fi settings, tap **Share**, and show your network as a QR code. Another phone scans it and joins. The iPhone camera can also join a network from a QR code, but I did not know of any way to make one on my iPhone.

So I asked myself: why not make it myself?

Later I learned that iOS 18 can do it too. But the feature is well hidden in the Passwords app, it only works for networks your iPhone already joined, and you cannot print the code as a sign for guests.

## In short

- The idea: a Wi-Fi QR code on iPhone, like Android has
- Built with Codex: first code on 31 May 2026, on the App Store on 4 June
- Other people needed it too, so I kept going
- Today: version 1.7, printable guest signs, 12 languages, still free

## A Wi-Fi QR code is a short line of text

A Wi-Fi QR code does not hold anything secret or special. It holds one short line of text, like this:

`WIFI:T:WPA;S:Hotel Guest;P:the-password;;`

`T` is the security type, `S` is the network name and `P` is the password. When you point the iPhone camera at the code, iOS reads this line and asks if you want to join the network. You type nothing.

So the app only had to do a few things well: keep my networks, put the right text in the code, and make the code easy to show and share. It looked like a weekend project. I thought it was an app that only I needed.

## Built with Codex, live four days later

I used Codex to build the first version. I described what I wanted, Codex wrote the code, and I tried each part on my own iPhone. The project started on **31 May 2026**. On the first day, the app could already:

- save Wi-Fi networks on the device,
- find the name of the network you are on, when iOS allows it,
- make the QR code and share it as an image.

The next day I made the design cleaner. The day after that, the app spoke 12 languages. On **4 June 2026**, Wi-Fi QR was live on the App Store. I put it there mostly so that I had it on my own phone.

## Then other people started to use it

I did not expect much. But people I never met found the app and downloaded it. A small tool for my own problem was useful to other people too.

That changed how I thought about the app. On that trip, I was the guest. But someone at the hotel wrote that card, and every host, café and office has the same problem. So most of the work after launch was for the person who shares the Wi-Fi:

- **Scan a password from paper.** Point the camera at a router sticker or a printed card, check the text, and save it.
- **Print a guest sign.** Put the QR code, the network name and the password on a card for a room, a desk or a front door.
- **Make the sign fit.** Long router passwords shrink and wrap, so they never run off the paper.

![Three printable guest Wi-Fi signs from Wi-Fi QR: Gallery Placard, Ink-Safe Editorial with a long password, and Concierge Ledger](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-1-7-release-notes/wifi-qr-1-7-guest-signs-1280.webp)

## Where the app is today

Wi-Fi QR is now at version 1.7. It has six sign templates and four paper sizes, it supports WPA and WEP networks, and it reads router stickers in English, German, French and Arabic. The [1.7 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-1-7-release-notes/) have the full list.

Some things did not change from day one. The app is free, with no ads and no account. Your networks and passwords stay on your device unless you share a code or a sign.

## What I took from it

- **Start with a problem you have yourself.** I knew exactly what the app had to do, because I stood in that hotel room.
- **Ship the small version.** The first version did one thing. That was enough to learn that other people wanted it.
- **Other people find uses you did not plan.** I built it for the guest. Most of the work since then is for the host.

If you have a Wi-Fi card on your fridge or a router sticker that guests always ask about, try it. Questions or ideas? Write to me through [Wi-Fi QR support](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/support/).

---

Source: https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-1-7-release-notes/

Release notes · Wi-Fi QR for iPhone

# Wi-Fi QR 1.7: guest signs that fit, WPA or WEP, and smarter sticker scans

A release about trust: the codes you make should always connect, and the signs you print should always show the full network name and password.

![Three printable guest Wi-Fi signs from Wi-Fi QR: Gallery Placard, Ink-Safe Editorial with a long password, and Concierge Ledger](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-1-7-release-notes/wifi-qr-1-7-guest-signs-1280.webp)

[Wi-Fi QR](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/) makes a QR code for your Wi-Fi network and turns it into a printable sign for guests. Version 1.7 came out on 10 October 2026. It does not add a long list of new screens. It makes the parts you already use more dependable. Here is what changed.

## In short

- Choose WPA or WEP, with clear checks under each field
- Guest signs fit long names and passwords on every paper size
- Print works from the share sheet
- Better router-sticker reading, including Arabic labels
- Guest passwords stay out of the iOS Passwords app
- Better VoiceOver, large text and Arabic layouts, plus many fixes

## Choose WPA or WEP, and see problems before you save

The network editor now has a **Security** picker. Most routers use WPA, WPA2 or WPA3, and that is the default. Older routers that still use WEP now get a code that works too. If a network has no password, turn on **No Password Required**.

The editor also checks what you type and tells you what is wrong, right under the field:

- A network name can be up to 32 bytes. Emoji and Arabic letters use more than one byte each, so the app counts bytes, not letters.
- A WPA password needs 8 to 63 characters, or 64 hex digits.
- A WEP key needs 5 or 13 characters, or 10 or 26 hex digits.
- If another saved network already uses the same name, you see a warning, but you can still save.

A QR code with a wrong password looks fine on paper and fails at the door. These checks stop that before you print. Networks that use a company login (enterprise Wi-Fi) also no longer get a code that cannot work.

![The Add Network editor with the Security picker and Scan Router Sticker, next to the guest sign screen with six templates and four paper sizes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/wifi-qr-1-7-release-notes/wifi-qr-1-7-editor-print-1280.webp)

## Guest signs that fit long names and passwords

Router passwords can be long, and some network names are long too. Before 1.7, a long value could run past the edge of a sign. Now the text gets smaller, step by step, until it fits. If it is still too long, it wraps to the next line.

This works on all four paper sizes, **4 × 6 in**, **5 × 7 in**, **A4** and **US Letter**, and in all six templates: Classic, Code Only, Gallery Placard, Concierge Ledger, Signal Grid and Ink-Safe Editorial. The middle sign in the picture at the top has a long router password on a 4 × 6 card.

## Print from the share sheet

Tap **Share Printable Guest Sign**, then choose **Print** in the share sheet. In earlier versions, Print could fail because the sign file was gone before the printer read it. The app now keeps the file until sharing is done. The button also waits while the sign updates, so you never share an old version after you change the text.

## Better router-sticker reading, now with Arabic labels

Tap **Scan Router Sticker** and point the camera at the label on your router. The app reads the text on your iPhone, finds the network name and the password, and shows them to you to check before it fills the form.

- It now reads stickers laid out as a table, where the label and the value are on separate lines.
- It knows more labels, such as SSID, Network Name, Network Key and WPA2 Key, plus German, French and Arabic labels such as اسم الشبكة and كلمة المرور.
- It skips lines it should not use, such as admin login, IP address and serial number.
- If you cancel the camera, you go back to the editor and keep what you typed.

## Guest passwords stay yours

Before 1.7, iOS could offer to save a guest Wi-Fi password in the Passwords app, as if it were a website login. The password field now tells iOS not to do that. The QR images and sign PDFs that the app makes for sharing are also deleted the next time you open the app.

## VoiceOver, large text and Arabic

- VoiceOver reads each template and paper card as one item and says which one is selected.
- Scanned passwords are not read aloud.
- At the largest text sizes, editor controls stack and wrap instead of being cut off.
- Arabic sign titles and paper size units now display correctly, and sign text follows the direction of the language.

## Smaller things you may notice

- Search results now have Edit and Print actions.
- When you delete a saved network, you can undo it.
- If camera access is off, the app shows you how to turn it on in Settings.
- Delete in a hidden password field removes a whole emoji, not part of it.
- If saved data is damaged, the app recovers your list instead of starting empty.

## Price

Wi-Fi QR is free, with no in-app purchases, no ads and no account. Your networks stay on your device. It runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS 17 or later.

## How to update

If automatic updates are on, your iPhone installs Wi-Fi QR 1.7 by itself. You can also open the App Store, find Wi-Fi QR, and tap Update. Questions or ideas? Write to me through [Wi-Fi QR support](https://yoloabdo.com/wifi-qr/support/).

Comparison · Quran on Apple TV

# The best Quran apps for Apple TV, compared (2026)

Nine Quran apps run on Apple TV. This post compares what each one confirms for the TV, what it costs, and who it suits. Every row has a source. Written by Abdelrahman Eita, 17 October 2026.

Disclosure: the author makes Sajdah, one of the apps in this list. Nobody paid for a place in the list, and there are no affiliate links.

## In short

- Nine Quran apps have a confirmed Apple TV version. Three are built only for Apple TV: Sajdah, Quran Mushaf TV and the Holy Quran TV!. Six are phone apps with a TV version.
- Sajdah puts recitation, the Quran text, prayer times with Athan, live TV and Top Shelf in one TV app. It needs the internet.
- Quran Mushaf TV shows the Mushaf page on the TV, adds translation and tafsir, and works offline.
- Ameen and Quran Pro say that you can listen to recitations on Apple TV.
- For Muslim Pro, Quran TV, Quran Radios and Quran+, the store page does not describe the TV app.

## How we compared

Every app was checked on 17 October 2026 in the US App Store. An app is in the list only if its App Store page shows an Apple TV entry with a tvOS version. The comparison covers the TV only: listening, the Quran text, live streams, prayer times on the TV, Top Shelf, ads on the TV and price. For a phone app with a TV version, a feature counts only if the page says it works on Apple TV; "Not stated" means the listing does not say, not that the feature is missing. Store ratings are left out, because a phone app's rating covers every device. The apps were not installed and tested on an Apple TV.

## The comparison table

| App | Type | Price (US) | Listening on TV | Quran text on TV | Live streams | Prayer times and Athan | Top Shelf | Ads on TV |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sajdah | Built only for Apple TV (tvOS 17+) | Free; Premium $2.99/month or $26.90/year | 200+ reciters | Verse sync free; word by word on selected reciters (Premium) | Quran radio and live TV incl. Makkah (Premium) | Yes, 13 Athan voices and Qibla (Premium) | Yes | No |
| Quran Mushaf TV | Built only for Apple TV (tvOS 16.4+) | Free; subscriptions from $0.99/week | Recitation with verse repeat | Madani Mushaf pages, translation, tafsir | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Yes |
| the Holy Quran TV! | Built only for Apple TV (tvOS 9+) | $4.99 | 1 reciter (Abdelbasit Abdelsamad) | Verse by verse | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not marked |
| Quran Pro | Phone app with TV version (tvOS 12+) | Free; one subscription covers Apple TV | Yes | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Ameen | Phone app with TV version (tvOS 17+) | Free, no in-app purchases listed | Yes | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Muslim Pro | Phone app with TV version (tvOS 13+) | Free download | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Quran TV (Muslims & Islam) | Phone app with TV version (tvOS 9+) | Free download | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Quran Radios | Phone app with TV version (tvOS 9.2+) | Free download | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |
| Quran+ | Phone app with TV version (tvOS 15+) | $7.99 | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated | Not stated |

## Which app fits which person

- One TV app for the whole home, with recitation, the Quran text, prayer times, Athan, live Makkah TV and Top Shelf: Sajdah.
- Reading from the Mushaf page, or weak internet: Quran Mushaf TV. It works offline; Sajdah does not.
- A free recitation player with no purchases: Ameen.
- Already paying for Quran Pro on the phone: its subscription covers listening on Apple TV.
- Already using Muslim Pro, Quran TV or Quran Radios: try the TV version.

## Apps checked but left out

These apps have no tvOS entry on their App Store page: Quran Majeed, Quran by Quran.com, Al Quran (Tafsir & by Word), iQuran, Ayah, MP3Quran and Tarteel. Quran Audio by Quran.com mentions Apple TV in its release notes, but its page lists no tvOS version. Al Quran Tv did not load in the US, UK, Saudi, UAE, Tunisia or France stores.

Release notes · Sajdah for Apple TV

# Sajdah 1.5.0: Live tab, Quran fonts and word-by-word recitation

Radio and live TV in one place, six ways to read the Quran text, words that light up as they are recited, and a calmer player built around the Siri Remote.

![Sajdah player on Apple TV showing a verse of Surah Ar-Rahman with its English translation](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-quran-athan-apple-tv-1280.webp)

Sajdah 1.5.0 is a big update for the [Quran and Athan app for Apple TV](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/). Most of it is about one thing: making the Quran easier to follow and read from the couch. Here is everything that changed.

## In short

- One Live tab for Quran radio and live Islamic TV
- Six Quran fonts, with Uthmanic free
- Word-by-word tracking on selected reciters
- A calmer player with one More menu
- Top Shelf cards on the Apple TV Home Screen
- The verse of the day in your language and a localized Adhkar screen
- Prayer time and Athan fixes, plus a new first launch

## Radio and live TV, together in one Live tab

Quran radio and live Islamic channels used to sit in two separate tabs. They now share one **Live** tab with a simple Radio and Live TV switch at the top. The tab remembers the section you used last, so your usual station or channel, including the live broadcast from Makkah, is one press away.

Merging the two also frees space in the tab bar, so every tab label now fits in all 11 languages. If a radio station cannot play, the list stays on screen and the station shows a signal-lost icon with a Retry button.

![Live broadcast from Makkah in the Sajdah Live tab](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-live-makkah-tv-radio-1280.webp)

_Live channels and Quran radio now share one tab._

## Read the Quran in the font you love

You can now choose how the Quran text looks, and the choice applies across the app. Pick a font in Settings, in the reciter settings, or straight from the player's More menu.

- **Uthmanic** (KFGQPC Hafs) stays free and remains the default.
- With Sajdah Premium you can switch to **Amiri**, **Scheherazade New**, **Noto Naskh**, **KFGQPC Nastaleeq** or **Lateef**.

Each font has its own size and line spacing tuned for the TV, and the end-of-ayah marker is drawn correctly for every font. Narrations other than Hafs keep their own script.

![The player More menu with speed, repeat, A-B repeat, sleep timer and the Quran font picker](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-memorize-repeat-fonts-1280.webp)

_The More menu gathers speed, repeat, A-B repeat, the sleep timer and the new font picker._

## Follow every word as it is recited

Sajdah has always highlighted the verse being recited. It can now highlight the _word_: each word lights up in gold as the reciter says it, and the words that follow stay readable.

Word timings cover the complete Hafs recordings by **Mishary Alafasy**, **Saud Al-Shuraim**, **Mustafa Ismail** and **Mahmoud Abdul Hakam**, most surahs by **Islam Sobhi**, and most surahs of **Al-Minshawi**'s mujawwad recitation. Timings are matched to the exact recording you play. Where exact timings are missing, Sajdah falls back to verse tracking instead of guessing.

Reciters with verse tracking now carry a badge, and you can filter the list to show only them. Word-by-word highlighting is part of Sajdah Premium.

![Featured reciters in Sajdah with Ayah tracking available badges](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-quran-reciters-1280.webp)

_Reciters with verse tracking are marked in the list._

## A calmer player

The player was redesigned around reading:

- The reading panel stays in the same place whether the controls show or not, and it blends with the scenic background behind it.
- The control bar is down to four items: Now Playing, play/pause, captions and More.
- **More** collects speed, repeat, A-B repeat, the sleep timer, continuous playback, focus mode, ambient mode and the font picker, each with its current value.
- Long ayahs show in full, and you can scroll long captions with the remote.
- Transliteration is now an optional subtitle that stays off until you turn it on.
- In ambient mode, press Select to show previous, play/pause, next and exit controls.
- The screen saver no longer covers the player while it is open, and Now Playing shows the reciter's photo.

Under the hood, many fixes make resume, seeking, repeat, A-B repeat and the sleep timer more dependable.

## Sajdah on your Apple TV Home Screen

Put Sajdah in the top row of your Apple TV Home Screen and Top Shelf now shows three things: where you stopped listening, the verse of the day, and the next prayer. Select a card to go straight back to the recitation, to Today, or to Prayer Times.

## The verse of the day, in your language

The verse of the day used to show an English translation in every language. It now uses a translation in your app language, such as Turkish, Russian, Urdu or Swedish, and in Arabic the verse appears on its own. If the hadith of the day has no translation in your language, Sajdah hides that line instead of switching to English. The full hadith reader still offers every available translation.

The Adhkar screen is now fully localized, and in Arabic and Urdu its previous and next controls follow right-to-left order. Translations of each dhikr are available in English for now. Arabic text across Today, Prayer Times and reciter pages keeps its letters joined, and dates and times use Arabic-Indic digits.

![Today screen with continue listening, verse of the day and hadith of the day](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-verse-hadith-of-the-day-1280.webp)

_Today: continue listening, the verse of the day and the hadith of the day._

## Prayer times and Athan

- Prayer times are now calculated in your location's time zone, so they stay correct even when the Apple TV is set to a different one.
- Every Athan now pauses Quran or radio first, including when Sajdah has stayed open since the day before.
- The Athan banner has a clear **Stop Athan** button you can always reach, shows which voice is playing and what resumes afterwards, and shows the Arabic prayer name next to the translated one.

## A simpler first launch

New users now start by choosing their language, then pick a reciter, and Sajdah begins with Al-Fatiha in that reciter's voice. If you already use Sajdah, nothing changes: the app opens where you left it.

## Smoother navigation

- Going back from the player returns focus to the surah you just played.
- Opening a reciter from Search keeps you in Search, and going back returns focus to the card you chose.
- The back button on a reciter page names the tab you came from.
- Shorter tab labels fit in French and Russian.

## What is free and what is Premium

Sajdah stays free to download. Every reciter, the synchronized Arabic text, one translation, surah repeat and the sleep timer are free. **Sajdah Premium** adds Quran radio and live TV, prayer times with Athan and Qibla direction, Prayer Room, ambient mode, all translations and transliteration, word-by-word highlighting, memorization tools such as single-verse and A-B repeat, playback speed and the extra Quran fonts. Settings now has a Premium section that lists what is included.

## How to update

If automatic app updates are on, your Apple TV installs Sajdah 1.5.0 by itself. You can also open the App Store on your Apple TV, find Sajdah, and choose Update. Questions or ideas? Write to me through [Sajdah support](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/support/).

Source: https://yoloabdo.com/blog/building-sajdah-apple-tv-journey/

Story · Building Sajdah

# The journey so far: building Sajdah for Apple TV

In January 2026 I started a small side project: a way to play the Quran on the biggest screen in the house. Nine months later, Sajdah is a Quran, prayer and remembrance companion for Apple TV. This is the story so far.

![Sajdah ambient Quran mode showing one verse of Surah Ar-Rahman on a dark screen](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-ambient-quran-mode-1280.webp)

## Contents

- Why a Quran app for the TV
- From QuraanTV to Sajdah
- The first months
- From player to daily companion
- Onboarding, four times
- The household prayer clock
- Reading along, word by word
- What the TV taught me
- What comes next

## Why a Quran app for the TV

A phone is personal. A TV belongs to the whole room. In many Muslim homes, Quran recitation plays in the background for hours, and the TV is often the best speaker and the biggest screen in the house. I wanted a way to fill the living room with recitation and let everyone follow the verses together, without passing a phone around.

The first commit landed on 27 January 2026, under the name **QuraanTV**. It already had a reciter picker, a player and verse timing. From the start I wanted Quran listening to be free and ad-free, something I hoped could be a small _sadaqah jariyah_: a good deed that keeps giving after the work is done.

## From QuraanTV to Sajdah

QuraanTV described the first version well: Quran recitation on a TV. Within weeks the app also had prayer times, the Athan and a Qibla compass, and the name felt too narrow. **Sajdah**, the prostration in prayer, points at the whole daily rhythm the app now serves: prayer, Quran and remembrance. You will still see the shorter spelling, Sajda, in a few places, including the address of [the app's page](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/). The code is still called QuraanTV, because renaming it would change nothing for anyone who uses the app.

## The first months: getting the basics right on a TV

February 2026 was about foundations: hundreds of reciters, verse sync, prayer times with a Qibla compass, the Athan at prayer time, and an interface in many languages, including right-to-left Arabic. At the end of the month came Quran radio and live Islamic TV. Today Sajdah speaks 11 languages.

Then came App Review, which taught me more than I expected:

- A QR code in Settings that pointed to a donation page was not allowed inside the app (guideline 3.1.1), even though the same link is fine on a website.
- An app's first subscription has to be submitted together with a new app version.
- tvOS apps need a privacy policy URL too.
- Rejection messages can be vague, so each round needs some detective work.

I turned several of these lessons into validation checks for the open-source App Store Connect CLI, so the next submission, mine or anyone else's, catches them before review does.

## From player to daily companion

The early app was a good Quran player, but people mostly opened it around prayer times. So in March, with version 1.3.0, the home screen changed from a grid of reciters to a **Today** tab: the next prayer with a live countdown, the Hijri and Gregorian dates, a verse of the day, and one press to continue the last recitation.

Morning and evening adhkar came with it, as a full-screen counter you press with the Siri Remote. In April a hadith of the day followed, drawn from Imam an-Nawawi's forty hadith, together with an ambient mode that shows one calm verse at a time for all-day listening.

![Sajdah Today screen with continue listening, the verse of the day and the hadith of the day](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-verse-hadith-of-the-day-1280.webp)

_Today turned Sajdah from a player into a place to start the day._

## Onboarding, four times

No part of Sajdah has been rewritten as often as the first launch. The first version asked people to pick an accent color, and on a TV that step trapped the focus: the Siri Remote could not reach the Start button. I removed onboarding, brought it back as a single screen, removed it again, and in 1.5.0 it returns in its simplest form. You choose your language, pick a reciter, and hear Al-Fatiha in their voice.

The lesson: on a TV, every extra step costs more than on a phone, and the first thing people want is to hear the Quran.

## The household prayer clock

Prayer times on a phone are personal. On a TV, they belong to everyone in the room. In August, Sajdah gained **Prayer Room**: six full-screen displays that turn the TV into a prayer clock for the home, switched with the remote's up and down buttons. The screen stays awake while Prayer Room is open.

The TV also changes how the Athan works. Apple TV has no notification banners to lean on, so the Athan is played by the app itself. That made reliability the real feature. In 1.5.0, every Athan pauses whatever is playing first, and prayer times are calculated in your location's time zone rather than the device's.

![Sajdah prayer times with a next prayer countdown, Prayer Room buttons and the Qibla direction](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/screenshots/sajdah-prayer-times-qibla-1280.webp)

_Prayer times, the Qibla direction and the doors to Prayer Room._

## Reading along, word by word

From the first version, Sajdah highlighted the verse being recited. The idea I kept coming back to was a step further: highlight the word. That needs precise word timings for each specific recording, so 1.5.0 bundles timings for selected Hafs recordings and matches them to the exact audio. Where timings are missing or unreliable, the app falls back to verse tracking rather than lighting up the wrong word.

The player was redesigned around reading at the same time: a steady reading panel, the current word in gold, only four controls, and one More menu for everything else. Six Quran fonts arrived too, with Uthmanic free for everyone. The [1.5.0 release notes](https://yoloabdo.com/blog/sajdah-1-5-0-release-notes/) cover all of it.

None of this would exist without generous open data: [Al Quran Cloud](https://alquran.cloud/api) for text and translations, [MP3Quran](https://mp3quran.net/api) for recitations, [Qur'anic Universal Audio](https://github.com/QUD-Technologies/quranic-universal-audio) for word timings, and [Aladhan](https://aladhan.com/prayer-times-api) for prayer times.

## What the TV taught me

- **Design for the remote, not the pointer.** Clicking around in the simulator hides focus traps. Every flow has to work with four directions and one Select button, tested on a real Siri Remote.
- **Give people time.** Player controls that hid after five seconds felt rushed. People read, step away and talk to each other. Forty seconds feels right in a living room.
- **Right-to-left is more than a mirrored layout.** The remote reports physical left and right, so in Arabic the app has to swap them itself. Arrows have to mirror, and letter-spacing breaks joined Arabic script.
- **Never fall back to English quietly.** If a translation is missing, hiding the line is better than English inside an Arabic or Swedish screen.
- **Time zones are part of prayer times.** Times have to be calculated in the place you pray, not the zone your TV happens to use.
- **The screen saver is part of the design.** On tvOS it can cover your app mid-recitation, so Sajdah keeps the screen awake while the player or Prayer Room is open.
- **Show the moment, not the feature list.** App Store screenshots that said "Fill your home with Quran" said more than a count of reciters, and on a TV the text has to be readable from the couch.
- **Small numbers mislead.** With a young app, a handful of people can swing any chart. I learned to wait for enough data and to keep my own test devices out of it.

## Free at the core

One decision has not changed since the first commit: listening to the Quran in Sajdah is free, with every reciter, and there are no ads. Sajdah Premium is an optional subscription for the extras, such as live TV and radio, prayer times with the Athan, Prayer Room, Quran fonts and memorization tools. It is what keeps the app growing.

## What comes next

A few ideas I am exploring, with no promises on dates:

- **Daily rituals:** gentle routines such as Surah Al-Kahf on Friday and Quran before bed.
- **Memorization sessions:** guided repetition for learning a passage together as a family.
- **Ramadan mode:** an iftar countdown and a daily reading plan for the holy month.

Sajdah has been shaped by the people who use it. If there is something you would love to see, [tell me](https://yoloabdo.com/sajda/support/). Every suggestion gets read.

# How Surfing Works: an interactive 3D explainer

Source: https://yoloabdo.com/surfing/

## Born in a storm

- Every wave you surf began as **wind** — often a storm thousands of kilometres away.
- Wind drags on the sea: ripples grow into chop, chop into **swell**. Stronger wind, blowing longer over more open water, builds bigger swell.
- Swell sorts itself into long, smooth lines that can cross whole oceans while losing surprisingly little energy.
- The twist: the water does not travel with the wave. Each drop just **loops in a circle** — only the energy moves forward.
- The loops shrink with depth. About half a wavelength down (the **wave base**) the water is almost still.

## Why waves break

- In deep water a swell never touches the bottom. It rolls along at full speed.
- As the seabed rises, the water loops scrape the bottom. The wave **slows down and grows taller** — this is called shoaling.
- The base drags while the crest keeps going, so the face gets steeper and steeper…
- When the height reaches about **0.8 × the water depth** it can no longer hold its shape. The crest pitches forward: the wave breaks.
- A **gentle slope** makes soft, crumbling waves. A **sudden reef** makes hollow, powerful ones.

## Anatomy of a wave

- Great waves do not break all at once. They **peel**: the break runs along the crest like a zipper. That is what lets you ride across it.
- **Peak** — the highest point, where it starts to break. This is where surfers take off.
- **Pocket** — the steep part right beside the curl, where the wave has the most power and speed.
- **Face** and **shoulder** — the open, unbroken wall ahead of you. It gets softer the further it is from the curl.
- **Lip** and **barrel** — on hollow waves the lip throws out over the face and leaves a tube of air: the barrel.
- **Whitewater** — the foam left behind the curl. Beginners learn here: it simply pushes you toward the beach.

## Beach, point or reef

- Where a wave breaks depends on what is underneath it. Surfers talk about three kinds of **break**.
- **Beach break** — waves break over shifting sandbars. Peaks pop up in different places and often peel both left and right: an **A-frame**.
- **Point break** — swell wraps around a headland and peels down the coast in long, even walls. The best for long rides.
- **Reef break** — waves jack up over shallow rock or coral. Hollow, powerful and consistent, but the bottom is close and sharp.

## Is it worth paddling out?

- A surf forecast is a recipe. Learn to read a few numbers and you will know if it is worth paddling out.
- **Swell height & period** — period is the time between waves. A long period (12 s or more) carries more energy, so waves break bigger and stronger than the height suggests.
- **Swell angle** — swell hitting the coast at an angle peels. Swell that hits straight on breaks all at once: a **closeout**.
- **Wind** — light or offshore (from land to sea) is best. Onshore wind makes it choppy and crumbly.
- **Tide** — changes the depth of water over the bottom. Low tide is often hollower and faster; high tide softer and fuller.

## How to ride a wave

- **Paddle.** Lie on the board, chest up, and paddle hard toward shore. You must match the wave’s speed so it can pick you up.
- **Pop up.** Hands under your chest, push, and spring to your feet in one move — front foot between your hands, knees bent.
- **Drop and turn.** Angle along the face instead of going straight to the beach, then lean into a bottom turn.
- **Trim the pocket.** Stay close to the curl where it is steepest. Rise and fall on the face to keep your speed.
- **Get barrelled.** If the lip throws over you, crouch low, hold your line, and ride out with the spray.
- **Kick out.** When the wave ends, turn up and over the back of it — then paddle back out for the next one.

## When to pop up

- Timing is everything. Pop up too early and the wave rolls under you; too late and it throws you over the falls.
- Look back as it comes and paddle hard — you want to already be moving when the wave reaches you.
- **Too early:** the wave has not picked you up yet. You stand on flat water, lose speed, and it rolls under you.
- **Just right:** the tail lifts and the board starts to glide down the face on its own. That is the moment — pop up.
- **Too late:** you are at the very top as the lip pitches. The nose digs in and you go over the falls.

## Surf smart, surf safe

- **Right of way:** the surfer closest to the breaking part of the wave (the peak) has priority. Everyone else waits.
- **Never drop in.** Taking off in front of someone already riding is the number-one rule broken in the water. It is dangerous and rude.
- **Rip currents** are rivers of water rushing back out to sea. Waves pile water onto the beach, and it escapes through deeper gaps between the sandbars.
- **Spot one** by the calm-looking, darker gap where waves are not breaking — often with foam or sand drifting outward.
- **Caught in one?** Do not swim against it. Stay calm, float, swim parallel to the beach until you are out of the pull, then let the waves bring you in.
